title: Local correlations in long-range dual-unitary kicked Hamiltonian chains
authors: Vladimir Al. Osipov, Marc Cedric Spyra, Jana Carolina Schumann, Thomas Guhr, Boris Gutkin
abstract: Many-body Floquet models with exact space--time symmetry, such as the kicked Ising spin chain (KIC), provide natural examples of systems with dual-unitary dynamics. The requirement of exact space--time symmetry is, however, highly restrictive, as it permits only nearest-neighbor interactions. Based on a pair of Hadamard matrices, we construct a wide family of dual-unitary kicked spin chains with long-range interactions. We show that local two-point correlations in such models propagate along the light-cone edges \( |n| = r|t| \), where \(r\) is the interaction range, and can be derived analytically for operators with local support. This approach is illustrated using the example of a kicked Ising spin chain with next-to-next-neighbor interactions.
summary: The paper constructs an extensive family of dual-unitary kicked spin chains featuring long-range interactions. It analytically proves that local correlations are strictly confined to specific light-cone edges defined by the interaction range. This provides deep insights into the spatial and temporal structure of quantum dynamics in highly symmetric, non-local many-body systems.
main_problem: The study investigates how local correlations propagate within long-range dual-unitary kicked Hamiltonian chains.
main_result: Local two-point correlations are found to propagate exclusively along specific light-cone edges, $|k| = r|t|$, and these correlations can be derived analytically for a wide family of such models.
method: The analysis employs techniques based on establishing spatio-temporal duality using Hadamard matrices and calculating correlation functions via transfer operators or direct trace manipulations.
model_or_system: The system is a generalized Kicked Ising Chain (KIC) extended to include long-range interactions ($r>1$) while maintaining the dual-unitary symmetry. The dynamics are governed by time evolution operators $U = \hat{U}_K \hat{U}_I$.
key_observables: Local two-point correlation function $C(n, m, t)$, and spectral statistics diagnostics like the ratio of consecutive level spacings ($r$).
important_parameters: Interaction range ($r$), coupling parameters ($J, h$), and time/space indices ($t, n, k$).
main_assumptions: The construction relies on adding fine-tuned pairwise interactions to maintain dual unitarity with long-range couplings; periodic boundary conditions are assumed for some calculations.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the vanishing of correlations outside light cone edges $|k| = r|t|$ and show spectral statistics matching COE predictions for generic parameters, deviating at integrable points.
paper_structure: The paper develops the construction of long-range dual-unitary models, proves spatio-temporal duality relations, derives the structure of the correlation function $C(t)$ using transfer operators, and analyzes its decay rates and spectral statistics.
why_interesting: This work provides a rigorous theoretical framework for analyzing dynamics in complex quantum many-body systems exhibiting long-range interactions while preserving special symmetries (dual unitarity), which is crucial for understanding transport and correlation spreading in engineered quantum materials.

figures.caption: Figure 1. Shown on the upper left is a single layer of the two-dimensional KIC with nearest-neighbor interactions. The upper right figure depicts the equivalent spin chain with next-nearest-neighbor interactions corresponding to r = 2. The model is dual-unitary for J = π/4. The lower panel shows a generalization of this construction, namely a dual-unitary spin chain in which all neighboring sites are coupled. The homogeneous case is obtained for J1 = J2.

Figure 2. The figure illustrates correlations ⟨Q1(0, 0)Q2(k, t)⟩between a pair of observables localized at (0, 0) and (k, t), k = rn+m points of the space-time, respectively. For a general kicked model with interactions between r neighbors correlations in the shadowed, blue (color on-line) region, |k| > r|t|, vanish due to causality if ⟨Q1⟩= ⟨Q2⟩= 0, see the left picture. For a dual unitary model, illustrated by the right picture, one has ⟨Q1(0, 0)Q2(k, t)⟩= ⟨Q1(0, 0)Q2(¯k, ¯t)⟩, where ¯k = rt+m, ¯t = n. As a result, correlations here vanish everywhere except light cone edges, |k| = r|t|, depicted by the two blue (color on-line) lines.

Figure 3. Two-point correlations between operators (27,28) for q1 = σz, q2 = σ0, q3 = σy, q4 = σ0, q5 = σz, q6 = σ0, q7 = σy, q8 = σ0, with parameters h = 1, J = 1, 5. The left picture (a) depicts correlations for the case J1 = J, J2 = 0, The right picture (b) depicts correlations for the case J1 = J, J2 = J, As one can observe, solely the correlations along the light cone edges (|n| = 2|t|) do not vanish in both cases.

Figure 4. The average value of ratio of consecutive level spacings (46) for the spectrum of the dual-unitary spin chain with the next-to-next neighbor interaction for N = 15, J = 0 (left) and N = 15, J = π/4 (right), respectively. The value of r is averaged over all values in the separate (translation) symmetry sectors of k = 1, . . . , 7 and shown as a function of h. Note that the graph is symmetric under reflection h →π−h. For generic values of h the data for ⟨r⟩fit the circular orthogonal ensemble (COE) prediction. The dips at h = 0, π/4, π/3 (left) and at h = 0, π/4 (right) correspond to spectral statistics characteristic of integrable systems.
